place.source_title: Selfridge Field, Building Nos. 246 & 253, 246 Birch Street

brief: Two-storey red-brick Georgian Revival house built from a standard Army Air Corps plan as noncommissioned officers' family quarters (a two-family unit, modelled here as one house) at Selfridge Field; hipped roof, a tall end chimney, 6/6 windows with soldier-course heads, twin pedimented entrance porches on slender columns and a glazed sunporch wing at the side; a swing set on the lawn.

floors: W W W W W W
facade.notes: a two-storey brick hip-roofed duplex (Selfridge Field, 1930): paired entries under a shared pedimented hood with iron rails, a white-framed enclosed sunroom at each end, 6/6 windows; shrubs along the foundation, an open lawn running between the quarters; neighbours of the same plan beyond

why.note: Army Air Corps officers' quarters: two families per building, a standard plan repeated down the street
1920s-30s military housing used Colonial Revival brick for dignity and economy (Quartermaster standard plans)
sunrooms at the ends: Michigan winters
